name: neurosync-evidence-sufficiency-eval
description: Labeled evidence configurations for measuring whether NeuroSync's transparent scoring correctly decides that a conclusion has sufficient supporting evidence. Each scenario is materialised as real Conflict/Hypothesis/Evidence rows and scored with the production app.services.scoring_service.score_hypothesis function.

expected_status_definition.supported: Multiple independent direct sources corroborate the hypothesis; it may be presented as supported.
expected_status_definition.review_required: A single source supports the hypothesis. The design contract states that one source is NOT independent corroboration, so the hypothesis must never be marked 'supported'.
expected_status_definition.inconclusive: Evidence is absent, or supporting and contradicting evidence are balanced; no defensible conclusion can be drawn.
expected_status_definition.contradicted: Contradicting evidence clearly outweighs supporting evidence.

evidence_weight_model: weight = 0.40*relevance + 0.35*reliability + 0.25*directness, clamped to [0,1]. Missing reliability defaults from evidence_type; missing relevance/directness default to 0.5.
notes: document_index refers to a distinct synthetic source document so that 'distinct source' semantics can be exercised.
These scenarios test a design contract (e.g. single-source support must not be 'supported'), not merely a re-derivation of the scoring formula.

scenarios.description: A hypothesis with no supporting or contradicting evidence at all.
scenarios.rationale: With no evidence the system must not claim any support; insufficient evidence cannot yield a supported conclusion.

scenarios.description: Three direct measurement items, all from one document.
scenarios.rationale: Repeated claims from the same source are not independent corroboration, so a single-source hypothesis must be flagged for review instead of 'supported'.

scenarios.description: Direct high-reliability items from three distinct documents.
scenarios.rationale: Independent direct corroboration from multiple sources is the intended basis for a supported hypothesis.

scenarios.description: One weak supporting item against two strong contradicting items.
scenarios.rationale: When contradicting evidence clearly outweighs support, the hypothesis should be marked contradicted rather than supported.
Balanced conflicting evidence must remain inconclusive; the system should not force a conclusion.

scenarios.description: A single low-reliability, low-relevance supporting item against two strong contradicting items.
scenarios.rationale: Unreliable, low-relevance support should not survive strong contradicting evidence; the hypothesis is contradicted.
